whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the Agentforce Life Sciences Consultant exam?

personas.label: Life Sciences Consultants
personas.description: You design Salesforce solutions for pharmaceutical, biotech, or medical technology clients.

personas.label: Salesforce Admins moving into Life Sciences
personas.description: You have Platform Administrator experience and want to work on life sciences projects.

personas.label: Business Analysts on Life Sciences projects
personas.description: You gather requirements for HCP/HCO engagement, territory management, and compliant field work.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Agentforce Life Sciences Consultant exam hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam tests how to set up compliant, data-driven interactions with healthcare organizations (HCOs), healthcare professionals (HCPs), and partners. It asks you to apply the features to a situation, not just recall their names.
bullets: 60 scored questions plus up to five unscored questions that do not affect your result.
Exam fee: US$200; retake fee: US$100, plus applicable taxes.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Before booking, practice setting up accounts and territories, an engagement plan, and a compliant HCP interaction without hesitation.

examFormat.heading: Agentforce Life Sciences Consultant exam format
examFormat.intro: The proctored exam has multiple-choice and multiple-select questions. You can take it online or at a test center.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Many questions describe a life sciences field or medical affairs team and ask how to set up territories, engagement plans, or Agentforce interactions.
bestWayToPass: Learn accounts and territories: Understand how HCOs and HCPs are organized and how territories determine field coverage.
Study engagement plans: Learn how plans and templates support repeatable interactions.
Understand Data 360: Know how it combines customer data and makes that data available to Agentforce.
Follow compliance rules: Know which choices support compliant HCP and HCO interactions.

expertInsight: Use Salesforce’s official exam guide and Trailhead preparation trail to study for this new 2026 credential. Focus on the current product and official courses (LSC001 and LSC002), since older Life Sciences Cloud material may describe features that have changed.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how to design and set up Agentforce Life Sciences for Customer Engagement. Topics include account and territory management, engagement plans, and compliant HCP/HCO interactions using Data 360 and Agentforce. The exam has 60 scored questions in 105 minutes and a 62% passing score.

keyConcepts.h2: Agentforce Life Sciences Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Account and Territory Management
blocks.body: Life Sciences for Customer Engagement organizes healthcare organizations (HCOs) and healthcare professionals (HCPs) under territories. This helps reps see who they can contact and where. Set territories and account hierarchies to match the client’s sales and medical affairs teams.

blocks.heading: Engagement Planning and Execution
blocks.body: Engagement plans define a repeatable series of interactions, such as product launch visits or calls and sample drops. Templates provide the reusable steps. Set templates to match approved interaction types, then track each plan as it is carried out.

blocks.heading: Data 360 for Life Sciences
blocks.body: Data 360 combines HCP/HCO data, interaction history, and consent in one customer profile. Agentforce can use this profile to personalize interactions. Make sure users only see data they are allowed to access.

blocks.heading: Agentforce for Life Sciences
blocks.body: Agentforce can suggest next steps or draft interaction summaries for field reps. Each suggestion must follow the same consent and compliance rules as a human-created interaction.

blocks.heading: Compliance and HCP/HCO Interactions
blocks.body: Life sciences teams must follow rules about what they can say, to whom, and how they record it. For example, decide whether a rep may edit a completed interaction based on compliance needs as well as general Salesforce security.

scenarioTips.h2: How to pass the Agentforce Life Sciences Consultant exam
scenarioTips.intro: Questions often describe a field or medical affairs team. Choose a setup that works for the team and follows compliance rules.

blocks.heading: Separate 'what the rep sees' from 'what the rep can do'
blocks.body: A rep may be allowed to view an interaction but not change its final record. Check what the user can see separately from what they can edit.

blocks.heading: Match the template to the interaction type
blocks.body: Choose an engagement plan template that matches the interaction, such as a sample drop or a medical information request.

blocks.heading: Trace data back to Data 360
blocks.body: When a question asks what Agentforce knows about an HCP, check what Data 360 has unified and whether consent allows its use.

blocks.heading: Watch for territory and hierarchy traps
blocks.body: If a rep needs access outside their territory, check the territory setup. Do not assume the role hierarchy controls this access.

blocks.heading: Don't assume general Health Cloud knowledge transfers directly
blocks.body: This product is designed for life sciences work. Some ideas overlap with Health Cloud, but territory and engagement-plan features are specific to this product.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Consultant Certifications
nextCertsAfter.intro: After this credential, round out your consultant track with adjacent industry and data certifications:

sampleQuestions.question: A field rep needs to know which HCOs and HCPs they may visit this quarter. What sets this coverage?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Account and territory assignments define which HCOs and HCPs a field rep covers.
whyWrong: Public Groups help share records generally; they do not set life sciences account coverage.
Chatter Groups support collaboration, not territory assignment.
Report folders control access to reports, not the accounts a rep can visit.

sampleQuestions.question: A client wants every sample-drop visit to follow the same five steps. What should the consultant set up?
options: A dashboard filter for visit reports
sampleQuestions.explanation: An engagement plan template provides the reusable steps for a visit sequence.
whyWrong: A validation rule checks field values; it does not define a series of visit steps.
An approval process routes a record for sign-off, not a repeatable visit sequence.
A dashboard filter changes the report view, not how a visit is performed.

sampleQuestions.question: Before enabling Agentforce next-best-action suggestions for HCP visits, what should the consultant check?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Agentforce suggestions for regulated interactions must follow the same consent and compliance rules as human-created content.
whyWrong: Grammar and style do not show whether a suggestion meets consent and compliance rules.
Response time does not determine whether the suggestion is compliant.
Brand style does not replace compliance review.

sampleQuestions.question: A medical science liaison submits a request that must stay unchanged for audit purposes. What should the consultant set up?
options: Hide it from the list view
sampleQuestions.explanation: Locking the record after submission helps keep the request unchanged for audit purposes.
whyWrong: Allowing edits after submission does not protect the record from changes.
Deleting the record removes the audit history.
Hiding the record from a list does not stop someone from editing it.

sampleQuestions.question: How can Data 360 support Agentforce Life Sciences for Customer Engagement?
options: Unify HCP/HCO data, history, and consent
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data 360 brings HCP/HCO data, interaction history, and consent into a profile Agentforce can use.
whyWrong: Data 360 works alongside account and territory management; it does not replace it.
Data 360 is not limited to marketing email.
Data 360 does not approve promotional claims.

sampleQuestions.question: A client requires pre-approved content for HCP visits. What design meets this need?
options: Let reps share any content without pre-approval
Use an approved library by interaction type
sampleQuestions.explanation: An approved content library limits reps to materials cleared for the interaction type.
whyWrong: Allowing any upload would not ensure that content was approved.
Disabling all sharing also blocks approved content reps need.
Personal email bypasses Salesforce controls and audit history.

sampleQuestions.question: A rep moves to a new territory mid-quarter. What changes?
options: The change waits until the next fiscal year
sampleQuestions.explanation: A territory change updates which HCOs and HCPs the rep is assigned to cover.
whyWrong: Changing territories does not delete past activity.
A territory change does not automatically change a user’s license.
Coverage changes with the reassignment; it does not have to wait for a new fiscal year.

sampleQuestions.question: How does an engagement plan differ from its template?
options: The plan is reusable; the template is one-time
The template is only for reports
Template is reusable; plan is applied
sampleQuestions.explanation: The template is the reusable blueprint; the engagement plan applies it to a real account or HCP.
whyWrong: The plan and template are different records with different roles.
This reverses the relationship: the template is reusable and the plan is applied.
Templates define the steps; they are not only for reporting.

sampleQuestions.question: An HCP withdraws consent for marketing. What should happen to consent-based Agentforce engagement?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Consent-based Agentforce engagement must stop when the HCP withdraws consent.
whyWrong: Agentforce must follow consent rules; it is not exempt.
Deleting the HCP record is not the right response and removes needed history.
Consent may apply across channels, not only email.

sampleQuestions.question: Why model clinics as child accounts under a hospital system?
options: Roll up clinic activity to parent
sampleQuestions.explanation: A parent-child hierarchy lets teams view and report on clinic activity under the hospital system.
whyWrong: A hierarchy does not create compliance reports by itself.
Territory assignments and account hierarchies serve different purposes.
The hierarchy does not change an HCP’s license.

sampleQuestions.question: A rep can see engagement plans outside their territory during UAT. What should the consultant check first?
options: Check territory assignment and sharing rules
Check Lightning page and field visibility
Review API version and integration settings
sampleQuestions.explanation: Territory assignments and sharing rules determine whether the rep can see those records.
whyWrong: Storage limits do not control record visibility.
API versions affect integrations, not ordinary record access.
A page layout controls fields on a record the user can already open.

sampleQuestions.question: How should Agentforce help draft an HCP visit summary?
options: Replace compliance review of promotional claims
Submit the summary without human review
Give the rep a draft to review and finalize
sampleQuestions.explanation: Agentforce can create a draft, but the rep should review it for accuracy and follow compliance rules before finalizing it.
whyWrong: A draft does not replace required compliance review.
The rep should review a compliance-sensitive summary before submitting it.
There is no need to delay the summary for 90 days; timely logging is the goal.

sampleQuestions.question: How can a client measure whether reps follow the approved engagement plan?
options: Report on plan and item completion
Survey each rep at the end of the quarter
Track completion in a separate spreadsheet
Use manager feedback from field visits
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reports on engagement plans and plan-item completion show whether reps follow the sequence.
whyWrong: Quarterly questions are hard to measure and do not scale well.
A spreadsheet moves tracking outside the platform’s reporting and audit trail.
Anecdotes do not give a consistent measure of plan completion.

sampleQuestions.question: What does Life Sciences for Customer Engagement add to general Health Cloud?
options: The products have the same features
sampleQuestions.explanation: Life Sciences for Customer Engagement adds account, territory, and engagement-plan features for life sciences field teams.
whyWrong: The products share a platform, but they are not identical.
Health Cloud supports more than payer use cases.
Life Sciences for Customer Engagement adds to broader healthcare capabilities; it does not remove them.

sampleQuestions.question: What should guide how long a life sciences client keeps interaction records?
options: Use a 30-day rule for every org
sampleQuestions.explanation: Record retention should follow the client’s regulatory and audit requirements.
whyWrong: Saving storage alone can conflict with regulatory retention rules.
A fixed 30-day period may not meet a client’s requirements.
A rep’s preference does not set the organization’s retention policy.

sampleQuestions.question: A pharma company wants each rep capped at a fixed number of product samples per month, with no way to exceed that cap. What should the consultant configure?
options: Sample Limits and Allocations for the rep
A Territory record with no limit field
A generic Flow with no sample-specific logic
A manual spreadsheet tracked outside Salesforce
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sample Limits and Allocations are designed to keep reps within defined sample quantities, exactly this requirement.
whyWrong: A Territory record organizes coverage, it doesn't cap sample quantities.
A generic Flow without sample-specific configuration wouldn't enforce the defined limits.
Tracking outside Salesforce defeats the purpose of configuring the system to enforce limits.

sampleQuestions.question: A regulator requires that sample distribution in a region follow specific documented handling and reporting standards. What should the consultant ensure the sampling workflow applies?
options: GxP standards appropriate to the region
No special standards, samples are unregulated
A general data retention policy with no regional variation
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sampling workflows must apply GxP (Good x Practice) standards aligned with regional regulatory requirements for sample distribution.
whyWrong: Sample distribution in life sciences is heavily regulated, not unregulated.
Personal judgment alone doesn't satisfy documented regulatory compliance requirements.
A generic retention policy doesn't address region-specific handling and reporting standards for samples.

sampleQuestions.question: A company needs to track a sample from when it's dropped off to a rep's trunk stock through final delivery to an HCP, with full chain-of-custody visibility. What process should the consultant configure end-to-end?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Sample Disbursement process manages the end-to-end lifecycle of a sample from distribution through delivery, providing the chain-of-custody tracking needed.
whyWrong: A Case record tracks issues, it isn't designed for sample chain-of-custody tracking.
A Content Workspace organizes CMS content, unrelated to physical sample tracking.
An Opportunity tracks a potential sale, not physical sample movement.

sampleQuestions.question: A compliance team wants periodic verification that recorded sample stock matches what's physically on hand, with discrepancies flagged for correction. What should the consultant set up?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Inventory Counting, Adjustment, and Audits are the configured capabilities for reconciling recorded sample stock against physical counts and flagging discrepancies.
whyWrong: A one-time email reminder isn't a repeatable, systematic audit process.
Territory reassignment manages coverage, not inventory reconciliation.
An Engagement Plan template structures visit activities, not sample stock audits.

sampleQuestions.question: Leadership wants ongoing visibility into total sample stock levels, usage trends, and potential shortages across the whole sales organization. What should the consultant provide?
options: Sample Reports and Dashboards monitoring the full sample stock lifecycle
A single static spreadsheet emailed once a year
No reporting, since samples can't be reported on
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sample Reports and Dashboards are built specifically to monitor the full lifecycle of sample stock on an ongoing basis.
whyWrong: A once-a-year static spreadsheet can't provide ongoing visibility into trends and shortages.
Verbal-only updates aren't a repeatable, auditable reporting mechanism.
Sample stock is explicitly reportable through configured dashboards, not excluded from reporting.
